correctness.rationale: A nonletter binary Lyndon factor starts in 0 and ends in 1. The one-marker class includes the singleton 1, while the singleton 0 contributes separately except for 111. For two markers the initial gap must exceed the interior gap; the two spans give disjoint sets since equal interior gaps make the second span empty. For three markers strict comparison with the last run requires i>c, and comparison with the middle run requires i>b or i=b>c. This proves the indicator correction including ties and zero gaps. The six disjoint integer chambers, with the first split by whether the middle gap equals the smallest, give the seven products and the correction at k=0. Uniform weak compositions of n−3 converge to the uniform simplex via lattice Riemann sums; the six strict orders are equiprobable and (3t,2x,y,d)/(n−3) is the constant-Jacobian simplex transform within each. The linear pieces give the stated mixture; averaging Dirichlet moments gives first moment 19/24 and second 37/45, hence variance 563/2880. The normalized counts are uniformly bounded; the nonconstant linear components have continuous distributions, with support up to 3. The independent rotation-based `python /workspace/reproductions/check_discrete_claims.py 4` checks 4845 words at n=3,…,19, the rational coefficients in that range and both moments exactly. Finite testing is only corroboration.
